newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk state Halkbank 96 net profit jumps 156 pct.
newsitem.headline: Turk state Halkbank 96 net profit jumps 156 pct.

text.p: Halk Bankasi, Turkey's second biggest state bank, raised its 1996 net profits to 5.9 trillion lira, up 156 percent from 1995, its general manager Yenal Ansen said on Thursday.

The bank's total assets reached 704.7 trillion lira in 1996, up 127 percent from 1995, Ansen said, adding that the real growth in total assets was 27 percent. Turkey's wholesale inflation was 85 percent last year.

The bank's total deposits jumped 144 percent, or 37 percent in real terms from a year ago to 561 trillion lira at end-1996, including 436.3 trillion lira of Turkish lira deposits which nearly tripled from 1995.
Ansen said the bank's lira deposit share in the banking sector rose to 14 percent in 1996, from 13.3 percent the previous year.

Halkbank's loans, extended mainly to small and medim-sized companies jumped 141 percent to 176 trillion lira last year and total placements surged 156 percent to 282 trillion lira over the same period.
Ansen said Halkbank's foreign currency assets were $1.5 billion at the end of 1996 when its short foreign currency position was zero.
He also said talks were under way with European banks for a new Eurodollar issue but did not reveal any details.
Halkbank launched 250 million marks worth of five-year bonds earlier this year without guarantee from the Turkish Treasury.
